title: Climate-triggered Institutional Price Pressure: Does it Affect Firms' Cost of Equity?
affiliations: University of Piraeus, Department of Banking and Financial Management and

detail.title: Climate-triggered Institutional Price Pressure: Does it Affect Firms' Cost of Equity?

publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis, forthcoming

detail.abstract: We document that climate-triggered institutional portfolio rebalancing affects S&P 500 firms’ cost of equity through climate change price pressure (CCPP). Using a demand-based asset pricing framework, we estimate firm-level CCPP from physical and transition exposures over 2005–2021. A one-standard-deviation intensification of CCPP raises the cost of equity by up to 6% of its average, with banks and insurers as the main drivers. Yet firms do not subsequently improve environmental performance, indicating that the statistically significant effect of CCPP on cost of equity is ineffective to alter corporate behavior. Our CCPP metrics can help policymakers and investors design targeted environmental strategies.

title: Reconceptualizing Food Environments Through Youth-Vendor Practices in Ethiopia: Implications for Policy
affiliations: , Haramaya University and Wageningen University and Research (WUR)

detail.title: Reconceptualizing Food Environments Through Youth-Vendor Practices in Ethiopia: Implications for Policy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Written and oral consent was obtained from all participants, and in line with ethical standards, parental/guardian consent was also obtained for minors. The study was ethically approved by the Ethiopian Public Health Institute Institutional Review Board (EPHI-IRB) under protocol EPHI-IRB-517-2023.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was part of the CGIAR Research Initiative on Sustainable Healthy Diets through Food Systems Transformation (SHiFT) led by the International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI) and the Alliance of Biodiversity International and the International Center for Tropical Agriculture (the Alliance), in partnership with Wageningen University and Research (WUR) and with contributions from the International Potato Center (CIP). We would like to thank all funders who supported this research through their contributions to the CGIAR Trust Fund: https://www.cgiar.org/funders/.

detail.abstract: Food environments (FEs) are central to debates on food systems transformation, but are often conceptualized as contextual determinants of individual choice. This study reconceptualizes FEs as dynamic configurations of practices shaped through everyday interactions, focusing on youth food consumption and vendors' selling practices in urban and peri-urban Ethiopia. Drawing on Social Practice Theories and Lived Experience Research, we employed photo-journals, observations, and interviews with youth and vendors to capture their diverse perspectives. Findings show that youth and vendors, through their everyday practices, actively co-construct and enact informal governance within FEs. Youth navigate tensions between health, socialization, and aspirations in their consumption practices, while vendors shape these spaces through care, credit, and informal hygiene regulation. These dynamics reveal FEs as relational, negotiated, and continuously performed, underscoring the need for policies that engage lived experiences rather than relying solely on top-down interventions. In Ethiopia and comparable LMIC contexts, recognizing the everyday governance enacted by youth and vendors can inform more responsive, equitable, and sustainable food system transformations.

title: State Fragility
affiliations: International Monetary Fund (IMF), International Monetary Fund (IMF), International Monetary Fund (IMF), George Washington University, International Monetary Fund, International Monetary Fund (IMF) and International Monetary Fund (IMF)

detail.title: State Fragility

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: The paper proposes a general conceptual framework for state fragility that aims to disentangle the identification of fragility from its underlying drivers. It reduces the identification state fragility to the responsiveness of its economic or political systems to shocks. In an extension of Taleb’s work, fragility is thus defined as a disproportionate (supra-linear) response to negative shocks and an underwhelming (sub-linear) response to positive shocks or to time. Consequently, the framework distinguishes between fragility to stress as breakdowns in political or economic systems in response to negative shocks and chronic fragility as the inabilty of economies to generate growth over time. The framework can be applied to both manifested fragility (where the list of fragile states it produces closely aligns with classifications by international organizations) and to latent fragility (where underlying drivers can offer a probabilistic proximity to a fragile response). We illustrate how latent fragility can be identified by focusing on coups d’état as reflective of political fragility: we use machine learning to examine coup drivers and their nonlinear interactions, and to derive implied coup probabilities across all countries. The paper parses out lessons for engagement with fragile states, especially on the importance of prioritizing the elimination of sources of fragility through strengthened structural fundamentals and the mitigation of stressors through stronger policies, both of which have higher returns in chronically fragile environments.

title: IDRIC Frontiers Report: Electrification
affiliations: University of Birmingham, Durham University, Durham University, Teesside University, Teesside University, Teesside University, Teesside University, Heriot-Watt University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: IDRIC Frontiers Report: Electrification
detail.abstract: Replacing fossil fuels in industrial processes with zero or low-carbon electricity has the potential to make a very significant contribution to industrial decarbonisation. This report brings together insights from six IDRIC research projects, along with a dedicated policy roundtable, to explore the potential, the challenges, and the future direction of industrial electrification in the UK.

title: Risk-informed credibility assessment for clinical AI/ML models: a practical methodology with an in silico trial case
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Risk-informed credibility assessment for clinical AI/ML models: a practical methodology with an in silico trial case
detail.abstract: ObjectiveData-driven models are increasingly embedded in healthcare settings and clinical decision support (CDS) workflows, yet credibility appraisal remains ad hoc—especially for artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) models whose behavior is non-deterministic and lifecycle-dependent. This work proposes a risk-informed methodology for credibility assessment that can be instantiated within in silico clinical trial (ISCT) settings and related clinical evaluation pipelines.MethodsThe framework formalizes three constructs—question of interest (QOI), context of use (COU), and model risk assessment (MRA)—and extends ASME V&V 40 with AI-specific dimensions (explainability, drift susceptibility, update dynamics). Evaluation is organized into five stages: data quality assurance, internal validation, external validation, scenario-based evaluation, and post-deployment monitoring. Stage-appropriate analyses include calibration assessment, decision-curve analysis, uncertainty quantification, robustness under perturbations, and drift detection. Governance-ready artifacts (checklists, risk-to-rigor tables, monitoring rules) support auditability and reuse.ResultsApplied to a published acute ischemic stroke prediction model, the methodology revealed gaps in external validation, subgroup-level calibration, and lifecycle monitoring, and clarified evidence needed for risk-appropriate deployment.ConclusionsThe framework operationalizes credibility assessment for AI/ML-based clinical models in a way that is extensible across applications, aligning with regulatory principles (e.g., Good Machine Learning Practice (GMLP), Predetermined Change Control Plan (PCCP)) while remaining domain-agnostic. By linking model risk to evaluation rigor and by providing auditable artifacts, it offers a practical route to more transparent, reproducible, and trustworthy biomedical AI evaluations, with clear paths to CDS/ electronic medical record (EHR)-integrated deployment.

title: Algorithmic Collusion Under Firm Specific Cost Shocks
affiliations: Texas Tech University

detail.title: Algorithmic Collusion Under Firm Specific Cost Shocks
detail.abstract: The increasing use of algorithms to make pricing decisions has begun to concern antitrust authorities. This paper considers a repeated differentiated product Bertrand pricing game where firm-specific marginal cost fluctuates over time. An experimental analysis of the behavior of Q-Learning algorithms is conducted. It is found that the algorithms autonomously learn to tacitly collude even in environments with fluctuating private costs, with the high prices sustained through reward-punishment strategies. Supra-competitive outcomes emerge without instruction, intent, or communication. The findings are robust to changes in demand and learning parameterization, as well as initial beliefs of the reinforcement learning algorithm.

title: Top-down Monitoring or Top-down Encroachment? How Centralized Tax Administration Undermined State Capacity in China *
affiliations: Peking University - School of Economics and

detail.title: Top-down Monitoring or Top-down Encroachment? How Centralized Tax Administration Undermined State Capacity in China *
detail.abstract: Centralized tax administration with top-down monitoring is regarded as a key element of the modern fiscal state. However, centralized administration can also introduce new agency problems for the monitors and create distortions across levels of the bureaucratic hierarchy. This paper studies how a fiscal administration reform aimed at monitoring local taxation can have unintended consequences on state capacity in late 18th-century China, using a novel dataset on tax collection constructed from administrative archives. We exploit predetermined variation across counties in exposure to the reform, which imposed formal oversight on county taxation by provincial treasuries. We find that the reform had a negative effect on tax collection. The decline in tax collection can be explained by a top-down encroachment mechanism: the reform created greater scope for monitors to withhold and misappropriate county funds. Such intergovernmental fiscal encroachment undermined local tax enforcement capacity and distorted county bureaucrats' incentives to underreport and embezzle revenue. We provide a range of evidence consistent with these causal chains.

title: Successful Voting in Weighted Committees and Shareholder Meetings
affiliations: , University of Bayreuth - Department of Economics and University of Bayreuth

detail.title: Successful Voting in Weighted Committees and Shareholder Meetings
detail.abstract: The applicable voting rule determines how closely collective decisions between three or more options reflect the preferences of a given individual. We construct measures of this and ask if a specific decision maker is more successful using plurality voting, plurality with a runoff vote, pairwise majority voting or the Borda scoring method. Our first benchmark finding is that if all voting weights are equal, then plurality rule maximizes the probability of obtaining one's individual top choice and Borda rule maximizes the voter-specific average ranking of the outcome. This result generalizes to asymmetric weights in aggregate terms but not from a single voter's perspective. We use computational methods to identify the individually most advantageous rule for any given weight distribution among three generic voters and also for the ten largest shareholders in S&P 100 corporations. Practical recommendations for the latter coincide in unexpectedly many cases with the analytical benchmark for equal weights. We also find that the Borda rule translates voting weights into voting success the most transparently and that traditional power indices for binary voting games approximate success in weighted committees well.

title: Justification Of Consequentialism

detail.title: Justification Of Consequentialism
detail.abstract: Consequentialism and deontology have long been two competing thoughts in normative ethics/economics. However, consequentialism should replace deontology for two reasons as follows. Firstly, the ultimate purpose of normative ethics/economics is to improve the outcomes for human being. A social norm is justifiable only if it improves the outcome. A deductive reasoning is justifiable only if it improves the outcome. Thus, only outcomes matter in normative ethics/economics. Secondly, deontology is another consequentialist way of thinking. We can clearly understand it, only if we imagine an unrealistic world in which the outcomes are reverse.

title: Direct Competition in the News Market
affiliations: University of Rochester

detail.title: Direct Competition in the News Market
detail.abstract: I consider a model of strategic communication between an uninformed voter and two informed and biased media outlets. Information can be fabricated but at a cost. I focus on the role of competition in the market for news where media outlets simultaneously deliver a report to influence the choice of a multihoming voter. In equilibrium, both media outlets reveal their private information with positive probability, and misreport otherwise. Even though competition can lead to more information distortions, it improves the welfare of the voter independently of the additional source's bias. The voter gathers better information on average because she can cross validate and rationally account for the credibility of news reports, thus mitigating the detrimental impact of biased information.

title: Digital Dirigisme: How Artificial Intelligence Reshapes Political Economy

detail.title: Digital Dirigisme: How Artificial Intelligence Reshapes Political Economy
detail.abstract: This essay examines the shift from market-based to model-based rationality in data-driven economies. Starting from Hayek's problem of knowledge, it argues that artificial intelligence (AI) technically overcomes the limitations of decentralized information gathering, thereby producing new forms of coordination. Markets that once operated through prices and experience are increasingly governed by algorithmic anticipation and machine prediction. From this transformation emerges a silent metamorphosis of political economy: control no longer proceeds through planning or competition but through the selforganizing dynamics of digital infrastructures. The essay designates this phenomenon as digital dirigisme-an order in which technical systems, through metrics of value and architectures of goals, de facto determine what a society deems rational, efficient, and desirable. Efficiency thereby becomes a principle of legitimation. The challenge lies in understanding this new form of algorithmic coordination politically, and in limiting it institutionally before it becomes autonomous through its own momentum.

title: The Policy Paradox of Biofuel Acceleration: An Analysis of India's E20 Mandate and the Citizen-Led 'Greenlash' Phenomenon

detail.title: The Policy Paradox of Biofuel Acceleration: An Analysis of India's E20 Mandate and the Citizen-Led 'Greenlash' Phenomenon
detail.abstract: India's early implementation of 20% Ethanol Blended Petrol (E20) reflects an ambitious push toward energy security, reduced dependence on crude oil, and improved farm incomes. The initiative has already delivered major savings to the national economy, yet it also reveals a sharp contrast between policy success and public experience. While official estimates suggest only minor mileage loss, many consumers report significantly higher efficiency penalties and accelerated damage to older vehicles. At the same time, largescale ethanol production places long-term stress on water and agricultural resources. These challenges have triggered rising public resistance, often described as a "green backlash," as citizens call for the freedom to choose non-blended fuel. This paper examines how a strategy designed for national benefit is creating hidden costs for individuals, and argues that the policy's sustainability depends on openly addressing vehicle liability, efficiency trade-offs, and the environmental limits of current feedstock models.

title: Retirement and Consumption Insurance
affiliations: Utah State University, Reed College, Clemson University - Wilbur O. and Ann Powers College of Business and Clemson University

detail.title: Retirement and Consumption Insurance
detail.abstract: We use a life-cycle model and causal empirical methods to study how individuals respond to changes in wealth and income. We show that endogenous retirement provides substantial consumption insurance. First, we use a simple model to show that individuals fully insure changes in wealth by adjusting their retirement date, keeping consumption constant, when wages and fixed costs of work do not vary with age. In a richer model, we show that the retirement margin still provides powerful consumption insurance to unanticipated wealth and income shocks. Finally, to assess the predictions of the theory, we estimate the effects of receiving an inheritance on retirement and spending. We find large increases in retirement and relatively modest increases in spending, supporting the idea that endogenous retirement insures consumption in practice.

title: Monetary financing produces neither high inflation nor miraculous fiscal multipliers
affiliations: University of Groningen

detail.title: Monetary financing produces neither high inflation nor miraculous fiscal multipliers

declarations.funderStatement: Dutch Organization for Sciences, through the NWO Veni Grant No. VI.Veni.201E.010

detail.abstract: I investigate the macroeconomic impact of money-financed fiscal stimuli when the central bank pays interest on reserves. I do so in New Keynesian models where government bonds and reserves are imperfect substitutes. Despite reducing funding costs for the consolidated government, I analytically show for several models that there is zero impact from money-financed fiscal stimuli on inflation and the real economy (relative to debt-financed stimuli). Afterwards, I relax the conditions behind this 'irrelevance result', and show that money-financed fiscal stimuli barely increase inflation and output.

title: The Dark (and Bright?) Side of Shadow Banking: Evidence on Bank Stability and Market Power
affiliations: CUNEF Universidad, Universidad de Valencia and Universidad Autónoma de Madrid

detail.title: The Dark (and Bright?) Side of Shadow Banking: Evidence on Bank Stability and Market Power
detail.abstract: This paper examines the effect of shadow banking activity on the stability of traditional banks. Using a panel of 5,559 banks across 27 countries during 2009-2023, we find that shadow banking activity adversely affects bank stability. However, the magnitude and direction of this effect depend on the specific economic function carried out by shadow banks. Our results show that shadow banking significantly influences both the asset and liability sides of banks' balance sheets, mainly through its effect on the volume of loans and customer deposits, thereby ultimately shaping bank performance. Employing a two-stage least squares (2SLS) estimation with an instrumental variable (IV) strategy, we show that the impact of shadow banking on stability operates through bank market power. To reinforce causal identification, we exploit the 2017-2018 Asset Management Reform Plan (AMRP) in China as a quasi-exogenous regulatory shock. Consistent with global evidence, the AMRP analysis confirms that restricting shadow intermediation enhances banks' resilience, expands lending capacity, and enables banks to attract greater deposit funding.

title: Impact of financial and energy market uncertainties on ASEAN-5 markets
affiliations: North South University, Linkoping University - Department of Management and Engineering Division and Norwegian University of Life Sciences (NMBU) - School of Economics and Business

detail.title: Impact of financial and energy market uncertainties on ASEAN-5 markets

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest
declarations.ethicsApproval: No ethical issues
declarations.funderStatement: CTRG Grant, NSU, Bangladesh

detail.abstract: This study investigates the interdependence between global uncertainty indices and ASEAN-5 equity markets. Utilizing the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) and the CBOE Oil Volatility Index (OVX) as proxies for global financial market and oil market uncertainty, respectively, we examine their connectedness with five major Southeast Asian stock markets (Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, and the Philippines). A time-varying copula framework is employed to model non-linear dependencies and extreme tail co-movements, and we complement this with risk metrics (Value-at-Risk and CoVaR) to quantify downside risk spillovers. Our findings reveal that ASEAN-5 markets are highly susceptible to spikes in global volatility, especially during crisis periods. Singapore and Thailand show notably greater sensitivity to oil-market volatility shocks, while Malaysia and the Philippines react more strongly to global financial uncertainty. We also uncover asymmetric tail dependence: negative shocks to global volatility indices exert a more pronounced contagion effect on ASEAN-5 markets than positive shocks of equivalent magnitude. The ΔCoVaR analysis further highlights that systemic risk in ASEAN-5 is amplified under heightened global uncertainty, underscoring the need for vigilant monitoring of uncertainty transmission. These results significantly impact policymakers and investors in designing tailored risk management strategies to mitigate regional contagion.

title: Back to Work or Back to the Maternity Ward? The Effects of Extending the School Day on Fertility
affiliations: Centro de Investigación y Docencia Económicas (CIDE) and El Colegio de Mexico - Centro de Estudios Economicos

detail.title: Back to Work or Back to the Maternity Ward? The Effects of Extending the School Day on Fertility
detail.abstract: While the mismatch between the length of the school day and the workday is known to be an important childcare gap for parents who are (or would want to be) in the workforce, the effect of policies extending the school day to reduce this gap on fertility is unknown. We estimate the effect of extending the school day in public schools on fertility in Mexico. Exploiting the staggered implementation of a nationwide policy directed to public primary and preschools and data on the universe of births, we find that the availability of "full-time" schools significantly reduced fertility after program adoption. Effects are fully explained by reductions in fertility among second and higher-order births (intensive margin), with null effects for first-time births (extensive margin). Effects are concentrated in areas with stronger labor markets and are likely driven by mothers returning to the labor market due to the extended school-day. Our results suggest that total effects of childcare availability on female labor supply may be underestimated if these effects on fertility are ignored.

title: Online Sports Betting in Greece: An Empirical Investigation
affiliations: Hellenic Open University

detail.title: Online Sports Betting in Greece: An Empirical Investigation
detail.abstract: Although international interest on e-gambling commerce is steadily increasing, studies about the online sports betting sector in Greece are very rare. Based on a web survey the present study, attempts to address this gap, by shedding light on the active sports bettors characteristics, preferences and patterns in Greece. A thorough analysis of 325 internet sport bettors reveals contingent relations between significant variables, while conclusions are drawn about the size of stakes placed and the punters motivations.

title: The Fallacy of Collective Supremacy: How Teamwork Ideology and Student-Centered Education Undermine Scientific Progress
affiliations: Shenyang Normal University

detail.title: The Fallacy of Collective Supremacy: How Teamwork Ideology and Student-Centered Education Undermine Scientific Progress
detail.abstract: Modern science and education have become dominated by an ideology of collectivism-the assumption that teamwork, consensus, and student-centered learning are inherently superior to individual intellectual effort. However, historical evidence demonstrates that major scientific breakthroughs have almost always been achieved by individuals who defied collective opinion rather than by large groups acting in concert. This paper argues that the current glorification of collaboration in research and education suppresses individuality, discourages dissent, and contributes to the theoretical stagnation of modern science. Drawing upon the author's prior analyses of microwave absorption theory and broader epistemological decline, this study critiques the pseudo-democratic logic that replaces expertise with consensus and truth with popularity. It concludes that genuine scientific progress depends on reinstating the intellectual independence of the individual and reaffirming the teacher's authority within education.

title: Climate Change and Environmental Governance in Nigeria: A Focus on North Central Region
affiliations: Federal University Otuoke, Federal University Otuoke and Abia State University Uturu

detail.title: Climate Change and Environmental Governance in Nigeria: A Focus on North Central Region
detail.abstract: This study examines the intricate relationship between climate change and environmental governance in developing countries, focusing on Nigeria's North Central region which has a population of approximately 25.4 million people. Climate change significantly affects key aspects of sustainable development including agricultural productivity, water resource management, health security, and biodiversity conservation which are vital for human and economic well-being. The North Central region was selected due to its ecological vulnerability, recurrent flooding, deforestation, and agricultural dependence, making it a critical zone for assessing governance effectiveness in climate adaptation and mitigation. The research assessed three core themes: (i) the effectiveness of Nigeria's environmental governance framework; (ii) the institutional, political, and socio-economic constraints affecting governance; and (iii) strategies for strengthening governance and enhancing resilience. Using a quantitative survey design with 400 respondents, data were analysed through descriptive statistics (means, frequencies, and percentages) and inferential statistics, particularly a multiple linear regression model to test the predictive influence of governance strategies (funding, capacity building, awareness, and anti-corruption) on environmental governance effectiveness. Findings revealed that Nigeria’s environmental governance framework is perceived as moderately effective, with significant disparities in assessments across respondent categories. Institutional weaknesses, inadequate funding, and political constraints emerged as the most critical barriers. Although the regression results were statistically non-significant (p > 0.05), they showed that participation (β = 0.37) and accountability (β = 0.29) were significant predictors of governance effectiveness. Strategies such as increased funding, institutional capacity building, and multi-stakeholder collaboration were identified as the most impactful for enhancing resilience. The study concludes that Nigeria must prioritize institutional strengthening, resource mobilization, and community participation to advance effective climate governance. A multi-stakeholder, cross-sectoral approach is recommended to align national climate commitments with local realities. Ultimately, this research contributes to policy reform discourse by providing evidence-based insights that can guide national and regional strategies for achieving climate resilience and sustainable development goals in Nigeria’s North Central region.

title: New stochastic dominance theory for investors with risk-averse and risk-seeking utilities with applications including solutions for the Friedman-Savage paradox and the diversification puzzle
affiliations: Asia University, Department of Finance, Fudan University, University of Macau, Dresden University of Technology - Faculty of Economics and Business Management and Viana do Castelo Polytechnic Institute (IPVC)

detail.title: New stochastic dominance theory for investors with risk-averse and risk-seeking utilities with applications including solutions for the Friedman-Savage paradox and the diversification puzzle

keywords: Stochastic Dominance; Risk Aversion; Risk Seeking; Utility Function; riskier Asset; Less Risky Asset

detail.abstract: In this paper, we first state some well-known problems including the Friedman-Savage paradox raised by Friedman and Savage (1948) who wonder why individuals would like to buy insurance as well as buy lottery tickets. To provide solutions to the problems, we first use the idea from Fishburn and Kochenberger (1979), Thon and Thorlund-Petersen (1988), and Chew and Tan (2005) to use two-way stochastic dominance to define the jorder risk-averse and risk-seeking utility that consists of both risk-averse and risk-seeking components and we call the utility AD utility and call investors with AD utility AD investors. Thereafter, we develop a new stochastic dominance theory for AD investors and we call the theory ADSD theory. We then develop some properties for the ADSD theory, including properties of expected-utility maximization, hierarchy, transitivity, and diversification, and properties under the additional condition of equal mean so that we can use the theory to get the solutions for all the problems and hypotheses we set in this paper. Applying the ADSD theory, we first get a new solution for the FriedmanSavage paradox. In addition, we find that AD investors could invest in both completely diversified portfolio and individual assets and, in general, buy any pair of both less-risky and more-risky assets. For example, AD investors could invest in both bonds and stocks, both bonds and futures, and both stocks and futures to get higher expected utility.

title: The Israeli Structural Model
affiliations: International Monetary Fund (IMF), The Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Government of the State of Israel - Ministry of Finance - Israel, International Monetary Fund (IMF), Government of the State of Israel - Ministry of Finance - Israel and International Monetary Fund (IMF)

detail.title: The Israeli Structural Model

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Israeli Structural Model (ISM), a New-Keynesian Dynamic Stochastic General Equilibrium (DSGE) model tailored to reflect key characteristics of the Israeli economy. The ISM incorporates diverse consumer saving behaviors and labor skills, a dynamic high-tech (HT) sector, international trade and capital integration, and comprehensive fiscal components. As an integral part of the Ministry of Finance’s (MOF) Forecasting and Policy Analysis System (FPAS), the ISM serves as a macroeconomic policy scenario analysis tool, aiding in policy discussions and decision-making. This paper illustrates the ISM's policy use by evaluating strategies for utilizing additional government revenue generated from the HT sector boom in 2022 and their macroeconomic impacts. It compares three policy options: accelerated public debt reduction, redistribution through transfers, and increased public investment. The findings indicate that increased public investment is the most beneficial strategy, in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic, accelerating GDP's convergence to its trend, reducing public debt to GDP ratios, and mitigating real appreciation and the impact on the most vulnerable population.

title: Shaping Services Trade
affiliations: International Monetary Fund (IMF), International Monetary Fund (IMF) and

detail.title: Shaping Services Trade

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the effects of withholding taxes on cross-border trade in services, using a newly compiled dataset covering the universe of bilateral service imports and withholding tax rates from 2005 to 2021. Employing a theoretical framework that highlights the role of withholding taxes in curbing base-eroding payments, the empirical analysis reveals significant effects, with estimated semi-elasticities of 4 for royalties, 1 for technical fees, and 1 for total service import.

title: Earthquakes and Emerging Market Sovereign Bond Spreads
affiliations: , International Monetary Fund (IMF), International Monetary Fund (IMF) and RMIT University Vietnam

detail.title: Earthquakes and Emerging Market Sovereign Bond Spreads

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study how sovereign bond markets respond to earthquakes in emerging markets, using data from 96 countries between 2012 and 2023. While earthquakes raise spreads on average, the effect depends critically on state capacity. In low-capacity countries, spreads rise sharply and persist; in high-capacity states, they remain stable or fall. These effects appear immediately, last several months, and are robust to multiple controls and placebo tests. Our findings suggest that markets interpret disasters not simply as economic shocks but as institutional stress tests, penalizing fragile states. Institutional quality, in this context, acts as disaster insurance.

title: Calculations Behind Lottery Valuations

detail.title: Calculations Behind Lottery Valuations
detail.abstract: I introduce a novel experimental design tracking experimental subjects' calculations when valuing lotteries. The calculations predominantly fall into three groups: expected values, linear functions of monetary outcomes, or those unmatched to lottery primitives. Calculations exhibit remarkable within-subject stability alongside substantial betweensubject heterogeneity. Calculations strongly predict valuations: subjects performing expected values-related calculations display near risk-neutrality, while on average, other subjects' valuations display extreme unresponsiveness to changes in probabilities. An analysis by calculation group reveals distinct behavioral mechanisms driving behaviors: adoption of expected-value calculations is consistent with the reductions in implementation costs from the provided calculator, while the linear functions of monetary outcomes are consistent with the theory of attribute substitution (Kahneman and Frederick, 2002).

title: Data Portability, Information Rents, and Credit Expansion
affiliations: Indian Institute of Management Visakhapatnam and University of Hyderabad

detail.title: Data Portability, Information Rents, and Credit Expansion
detail.abstract: We study whether consumer-directed data portability expands the supply of credit or merely reallocates lending relationships. Extending Rajan (1992), we model how verifiable, consent-based data sharing lowers lending thresholds when the verification surplus exceeds marginal implementation costs. Using India's Account Aggregator (AA) system, a nationwide, read-only open-finance infrastructure, we exploit staggered institution-level adoption by banks and non-bank financial companies between 2018 and 2025. Employing modern difference-indifferences estimators suited to heterogeneous adoption timing, we find that AA adoption significantly increases retail and priority-sector lending, compresses loan spreads, and does not raise default risk. Non-banks expand proportionally more, consistent with lower marginal costs of verifiability. The evidence indicates that verified data access relaxes information frictions, enhances allocative efficiency, and scales both banks and non-banks, providing the first institution-level evidence that open-finance infrastructure can jointly promote financial inclusion and stability.

title: Emerging Market Cycles
affiliations: Reserve Bank of India, Reserve Bank of India and International Monetary Fund (IMF)

detail.title: Emerging Market Cycles

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper empirically examines the dynamic linkages between financial conditions and economic growth across 18 major emerging market economies over the last two decades and the role that fiscal and trade balances play in shaping such associations. Using a reduced-form multivariate autoregressive state-space model, we document two opposing forces – growth-enhancing and growth-inhibiting linkages – that characterize macro-financial dynamics in these countries. Easing of domestic financial conditions is associated with stronger near-term GDP growth, a growth-enhancing link, albeit this acceleration in growth is followed by a tightening of financial conditions that can adversely impact future growth outcomes, a growth-inhibiting link. Both linkages are statistically significant at high frequencies for nearly half of the countries in our sample and appear to be driven by a weak twin-balance sheets condition of high public debt and external imbalances. External factors, notably the global financial cycle, are shown to play a crucial role in amplifying this feedback loop between economic growth and financial conditions.

title: Modeling and Forecasting Bitcoin Volatility: A Comparative Analysis of GARCH and GJR-GARCH Models
affiliations: University of Sindh

detail.title: Modeling and Forecasting Bitcoin Volatility: A Comparative Analysis of GARCH and GJR-GARCH Models

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I, Waseem Khoso, declare that this manuscript is my original research work and has not been published elsewhere. All analyses, data interpretations, and conclusions are independently conducted for academic and research purposes.

detail.abstract: This study conducts a comparative analysis of GARCH-family models to capture the volatility dynamics of Bitcoin. Utilizing a comprehensive dataset of daily Bitcoin prices, we find that the return series exhibits classic financial stylized facts, including stationarity, leptokurtosis, and negative skewness. Through rigorous model selection criteria and diagnostic testing, the GARCH(1,3) model demonstrates a marginally superior fit compared to the asymmetric GJR-GARCH(1,1) model. Intriguingly, the leverage effect parameter in the GJR-GARCH model is statistically insignificant, suggesting that during our sample period, Bitcoin's volatility response to positive and negative news shocks was largely symmetric. Our findings provide critical insights for risk managers and financial analysts modeling cryptocurrency volatility.

title: Playing It Safe: Financial Sustainability of European Listed Founding Family Firms
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Marburg - School of Business & Economics and University of Marburg - School of Business & Economics

detail.title: Playing It Safe: Financial Sustainability of European Listed Founding Family Firms
detail.abstract: We are interested in founding family firms' willingness to investment in financial sustainability, defined as the capacity to meet long-term obligations and reduce refinancing and insolvency risks. Consistent with founding families' socioemotional wealth and intergenerational transfer motives, we document that founding family firms exhibit significantly higher levels of financial sustainability than other firms. We further examine how outside investors value such investments and find that founding family firms benefit more from financial sustainability than other firms. Our findings highlight financial sustainability as an important channel through which ownership structure shapes firm value.

title: Parameter Proliferation in Nowcasting
affiliations: International Monetary Fund (IMF), International Monetary Fund (IMF), International Monetary Fund (IMF), Princeton University and International Monetary Fund (IMF)

detail.title: Parameter Proliferation in Nowcasting

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper evaluates three approaches to address parameter proliferation issue in nowcasting:  (i) variable selection using adjusted stepwise autoregressive integrated moving average with exogenous variables (AS-ARIMAX); (ii) regularization in machine learning (ML); and (iii) dimensionality reduction via principal component analysis (PCA). Utilizing 166 variables, we estimate our models from 2007Q2 to 2019Q4 using rolling-window regression, while applying these three approaches. We then conduct a pseudo out-of-sample performance comparison of various nowcasting models—including Bridge, MIDAS, U-MIDAS, dynamic factor model (DFM), and machine learning techniques including Ridge Regression, LASSO, and Elastic Net to predict China's annualized real GDP growth rate from 2020Q1 to 2023Q1. Our findings suggest that the LASSO method outperform all other models, but only when guided by economic judgment and sign restrictions in variable selection. Notably, simpler models like Bridge with AS-ARIMAX variable selection yield reliable estimates nearly comparable to those from LASSO, underscoring the importance of effective variable selection in capturing strong signals.

title: Mauritius QPM
affiliations: , , , , , , International Monetary Fund (IMF),  and International Monetary Fund (IMF)

detail.title: Mauritius QPM

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper presents the Mauritius Quarterly Projection Model (QPM), the semi-structural analytical tool that underpins the modernized Forecasting and Policy Analysis System of the Bank of Mauritius (BOM). The model is designed to capture the salient features of the domestic economy, including key monetary policy transmission channels and the recently introduced flexible inflation targeting framework. Relative to canonical QPM structures, it also incorporates a parsimonious fiscal block and a labor market block, providing key insights on broader macroeconomic dynamics and enriching the policy advice. The model optimally balances theoretical consistency—evident in coherent shock propagation and policy responses—and empirical reliability, as reflected in its strong in-sample forecasting performance. The practical use of the Mauritius QPM in the context of the BOM’s regular forecasting cycles for the production of baseline projections, counterfactual simulations and alternative scenarios, together with the corresponding model-based economic narratives, make it a critical component of the BOM’s forward-looking monetary policy formulation.

title: Enhancing Tax Capacity
affiliations: International Monetary Fund (IMF), International Monetary Fund (IMF) and International Monetary Fund (IMF)

detail.title: Enhancing Tax Capacity

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Building on previous studies, we propose a robust estimation strategy to uncover the causal effects of tax administration strength on tax revenue in 121 countries over the period 2014–2022. Our novel approach utilizes a unique expert survey to construct an Operational Strength Index of tax administration, using the International Survey on Revenue Administration (ISORA), and employs an instrumental variable strategy based on the IMF Fiscal Affairs Department’s Capacity Development programs. We find that strengthening tax administration significantly boosts tax revenue, particularly in emerging and developing economies, and especially in countries with lower levels of informality, stronger institutions, and higher financial development. These findings carry important policy implications for governments and development partners aiming to enhance tax administration capacity and strengthen public finances overall.

title: Central Banks' Contribution to Financial Stability: From Central Bank Money Issuance to Macroprudential Supervision
affiliations: Swiss National Bank - Financial Stability

detail.title: Central Banks' Contribution to Financial Stability: From Central Bank Money Issuance to Macroprudential Supervision
detail.abstract: We define financial stability as a condition where the financial sector and its individual entities fulfill their macroeconomic functions. Banks, for example, are supposed to conduct liquidity and maturity transformation and create liquidity for the real economy. Financial stability does not emerge automatically out of individual agents' actions, but requires collective action. To create this public good, different stakeholders are necessary. Central banks have always played a central role due to their monopoly to issue central bank money, both in ordinary and emergency times. However, the contribution of central banks to financial stability extends beyond this. Today, they typically engage in macroprudential supervision, contribute to financial sector regulation, and, in some cases, have macroprudential tools such as countercyclical capital buffers at their disposal. Many central banks also have microprudential supervisory mandates, which are not covered in this chapter. Looking ahead, two issues appear to be of key importance for central banks in the context of financial stability: first, the role of central bank money issuance in the age of digitalization and against the backdrop of growing non-bank financial intermediaries (NBFIs) and, second, the precise meaning and scope of macroprudential supervision, not least to avoid regulatory fallacies.

title: Investment Security and Investment Attractiveness of the Ibero-America Countries
affiliations: MGIMO University

detail.title: Investment Security and Investment Attractiveness of the Ibero-America Countries
detail.abstract: Investment policy and investment strategies in global markets are a very relevant research topic due, on the one hand, to the tightening rhetoric of sanctions restrictions for different countries of the world and the increasing trend of protectionist economic policies of these countries, on the other hand, the inevitability of searching for investment opportunities and developing investment attraction scenarios to ensure economic growth, industrial development and technological leadership. Investment security as a tool is necessary not only to increase the inflow of investments (which do not bring threats of technological monopolism or pressure from foreign entities), but also to ensure the safety of investor's control over the assets at his disposal. But at the same time, investments serve as the basis for the technological sovereignty formation and are capable of both supporting and limiting the achievement of sovereignty. It is proved that, despite the diversity of approaches to national models of technological development and investment security, the statement remains unshakable that changes are based on investment potential. It is determined that for the countries of Ibero-America, the export-raw material model may be more attractive than in the conditions of increasing globalism, and such a model has the right to be considered in conditions of targeted control over the distribution of income from the sale of resources to achieve sovereign goals. At the same time, it is possible to expand the system of investment security indicators based on the coordination of the goals of states, business and society on the way to achieving economic growth.

title: Ties That Bind, Costs That Fall? CEO-Board Connections and the Cost of Debt

detail.title: Ties That Bind, Costs That Fall? CEO-Board Connections and the Cost of Debt
detail.abstract: This study examines how CEO-board connections influence firms' cost of debt, drawing on competing governance perspectives regarding the role of board friendliness. The role conflict view suggests that close social ties between CEOs and directors weaken monitoring, reduce corporate investment in valuable risky projects (due to managerial conservatism), and lower borrowing costs, while the role alignment view argues that such ties enhance monitoring through trust and information flow, which may increase investment in valuable risky projects, and consequently raise debt costs by shifting the risk from shareholders to bondholders. To evaluate these perspectives, I combine a stacked difference-indifferences design with instrumental variable analyses exploiting exogenous, CEO turnover-driven shocks to CEO-board connections, and a Heckman two-step procedure to address potential sample selection bias. Results show that CEO-board connections are negatively associated with firms' bond spreads, consistent with the role conflict view. Establishing channel, I show that this relationship operates through reduced corporate risk-taking, measured by the volatility of returns and leverage. Moreover, the negative effect of CEO-board connections on debt costs is amplified in nuanced information environments (specifically, when analyst coverage is high, forecast error is high, or both conditions jointly hold). Together, these findings demonstrate that interpersonal dynamics within the boardroom have material implications for debt pricing. The study contributes to the literature by clarifying the conditions under which friendly boards lower financing costs, and it adds to practice by identifying a novel governance channel that creditors can incorporate into credit risk assessments.

title: On Risk Pricing and Arbitrage in the Cryptomarket
affiliations: Université de Rennes 1, Université de Rennes 1, Université de Rennes 1, Univ Rennes, CNRS, CREM - UMR6211, F-35000 Rennes (France) and Université de Rennes 1

detail.title: On Risk Pricing and Arbitrage in the Cryptomarket
detail.abstract: This paper constitutes a tentative step towards factor investing in cryptocurrencies, adopting a stance that exploits market mispricing and risk timing. In the spirit of the Arbitrage Pricing Theory (APT), we examine the risk exposure profile (beta) of a panel of 29 coins to 8 risk factors. We study price anomalies through high-minus-low (High-beta returns minus Low-beta returns) portfolios and offer a tentative approximation of risk premia. The risk exposure profile reveal distinct classifications of coins with respect to systematic risks. The HML portfolios shed light on the extent to which market participants allocate weights to risk factors and on the resulting pricing differentials among cryptocurrencies. In this sense, they reveal underlying market risk preferences and highlight the potential benefits of long–short strategies. The estimated premia confirm the distinction between factors for which investors demand remuneration for bearing risk and those that carry negative premia. We introduce a dynamic optimisation architecture that adjusts factor exposure through a time-varying penalty. It implements a profitable factor-tilting strategy whose signal is extracted from a chartist analysis of the HML portfolios. Overall, this exploration offers valuable insights for portfolio design. It provides guidance for fundamental analysis through a detailed risk exposure profile. It showcase chartist signal extraction, evidencing that the HML portfolios act as effective risk trackers, to illustrate informed tactical allocation through factor tilting.

title: Teacher transfers: equalizing deficits across schools
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Indian Statistical Institute, Columbia University, University of Liverpool Management School and

detail.title: Teacher transfers: equalizing deficits across schools
detail.abstract: The Right to Free and Compulsory Education Act (2009) (RTE) of the Government of India prescribes student-teacher ratios for state-run schools. One method advocated by the Act to achieve its goals is the redeployment of teachers from surplus to deficit (in teacher strength) schools. We consider a model where teachers can either remain in their initially assigned schools or be transferred to a deficit school in their acceptable set. The planner's objective is specified in terms of the post-transfer deficit vector that can be achieved. We show that there exists a transfer whose post-transfer deficit vector Lorenz dominates all achievable post-transfer deficit vectors. We provide a two-stage algorithm to derive the Lorenz-dominant post-transfer deficit vector, and show that this algorithm is strategy-proof for teachers.

title: The Law of Monetary Equilibrium: The Efficient Reserve-Anchored Persistence (ERAP) Framework for Price Stability

title: Recovering Preferences from Mistakes: An Auxiliary Task Approach

detail.title: Recovering Preferences from Mistakes: An Auxiliary Task Approach
detail.abstract: Risk preferences recovered from lottery valuation data are not robust to unverifiable assumptions about the structure of mistakes in the valuations. To address this, we develop a novel approach utilizing Oprea's (2024) deterministic mirrors-deterministic payments that preserve key structural features of lotteries. We estimate the mistake structure in deterministic mirrors-where certain payments enable identification of mistake patterns-through a mixture model incorporating two types of mistakes frequently observed, then apply these estimates to correct lottery valuations. The corrected valuations are closer to risk neutrality than raw valuations; when they deviate from risk neutrality, they are predominantly risk averse. These patterns align the corrected valuations with expected utility theory, in contrast to the raw valuations which exhibit strong probability weighting. Our approach offers a generalizable framework for preference recovery: researchers can use auxiliary tasks with known correct answers to discipline assumptions about mistakes.

title: British Home Children in Canada: The Assimilation of Unaccompanied Minors *
affiliations: Department of Economics, Queen's University, Wilfrid Laurier University and Royal Military College of Canada

detail.title: British Home Children in Canada: The Assimilation of Unaccompanied Minors *
detail.abstract: In this paper we study the economic outcomes of foreign born men who arrived in Canada between 1869 and 1921 as unaccompanied minors. The Home Children who are the focus of our study were brought to Canada as part of an effort by charitable and religious organizations to improve living conditions for disadvantaged urban youth in Britain. We find that on average, men who arrived in Canada as Home Children were at a severe and persistent earnings disadvantage relative to observationally equivalent native born workers and other British born men who arrived as minors accompanied by their families. However, we also find that the assimilation experiences of the Home Children were highly variable-earnings penalties were smaller and assimilation rates were faster for the Home Children who were occupationally and geographically mobile, and the Home Children who enjoyed more careful placement and greater monitoring effort experienced more rapid earnings convergence.

title: Bank Runs without a Cause: Frequency, Contagion, and Mitigation Measures in the U.S., 1889-1929
affiliations: and Middle Tennessee State University - Department of Economics and Finance

detail.title: Bank Runs without a Cause: Frequency, Contagion, and Mitigation Measures in the U.S., 1889-1929

declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: No dedicated funding was received to support this work.

detail.abstract: How frequent and contagious were bank runs without a cause in the United States? We introduce a novel dataset of bank runs in the United States from 1889 to 1929, compiled from digitized historical newspapers, to examine the frequency, geographic distribution, causes, duration, and characteristics of bank runs during a formative period in U.S. financial history. Due to the lack of institution-specific reporting, we exclude the Panic of 1893, the Panic of 1907, and the Financial Crisis of 1914. Outside of these panics, we record 273 no-cause runs, an average of 6.8 per year. Slightly over 79% of these runs were averted within an average of 2.23 days. Only five non-cause runs spread to a total of 13 additional banks. While our data confirm the use of previously identified run-mitigation mechanisms, including clearinghouse associations, suspension of redemption, information disclosures, and changes in management, we detail additional common mechanisms: 1) the noninvocation of the redemption clause, 2) forfeiture of interest, 3) passbook speculation, 4) direct loans from financial institutions, 5) assurances from community, business, financial, and governmental institutions, 6) prominent displays of reserves, 7) modified banking hours, 8) unique clearinghouse association roles, and 9) reorganization. Our paper provides new insights into our understanding of early bank runs.

title: When Silicon Valley Meets Wall Street: A Theory of Financial Overengineering
affiliations: Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST) - Department of Finance and University of Lausanne - School of Economics and Business Administration (HEC-Lausanne)

detail.title: When Silicon Valley Meets Wall Street: A Theory of Financial Overengineering
detail.abstract: We study a model of financial markets with asymmetric information, in which a trading firm hires a financial engineer to develop proprietary technology to obtain an informational edge. The signal produced through this hiring is firmspecific and non-contractible, leading to a bilateral monopoly in wage determination. The model admits multiple self-fulfilling equilibria in technology innovation. In one equilibrium, excessive and inefficient innovation arises due to technological opacity and misaligned incentives between the firm and the engineer. The model connects financial market outcomes to contractual frictions in the finance industry and yields novel empirical implications for identifying inefficiencies in financial technology investment.

title: Implementing the Multilateral Instrument in India -The Notification Conundrum
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Implementing the Multilateral Instrument in India -The Notification Conundrum
detail.abstract:
In the Sky High Leasing Co. Ltd. v. ACIT  [2025] ITA No. 1198/Mum/2025, the Indian Income-tax Appellate Tribunal examined whether, in the absence of a separate protocol or notification amending the concerned double tax avoidance agreement (DTAA), the principal purpose test provision in the MLI can be read to restrict or alter the benefits otherwise available under the DTAA. The ruling followed the India Supreme Court ruling in Nestlé, SA, [Civil Appeal No. 1420 of 2023] which dealt with the most favored nation clause in India’s treaties. 

This article provides a brief description of the constitutional requirements in India to enter into treaties and grant them the force of law. It then examines the notification requirement under Indian domestic law to implement tax treaties and their revisions, particularly in the context of the MLI signed by India.

title: Comparison of Oracles: Part I
affiliations: Ben Gurion University of the Negev, Durham University Business School and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Comparison of Oracles: Part I
