title: Information-Minimized Stationary Financial Market Dynamics
affiliations: University of Technology, Sydney (UTS) - Finance Discipline Group

detail.title: Information-Minimized Stationary Financial Market Dynamics
detail.abstract: The paper derives the dynamics of a financial market from basic mathematical principles. It models the market dynamics using independent stationary scalar diffusions, assumes the existence of the growth optimal portfolio (GOP), interprets the market as a communication system, and minimizes, in an information-theoretical sense, the self-information of the stationary densities of the stationary scalar diffusions, and minimizes the Kullback-Leibler divergence of the benchmark-neutral pricing measure from the real-world probability measure. In the information-minimized market, its basic independent securities, their sums, the minimum variance portfolio, the GOP of the basic risky securities, and the GOP of the entire market are shown to evolve as squared radial Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes.

title: Africonomics and the Rebirth of Civilization: A Moral Vision for a Truly Civilized World
affiliations: Afrindependent Institute

detail.title: Africonomics and the Rebirth of Civilization: A Moral Vision for a Truly Civilized World
detail.abstract: This paper challenges the prevailing conception of civilization—defined by material progress, technological prowess, and domination under the Western worldview—demonstrating that it is narrow, mechanistic, and fundamentally flawed. It offers a redefinition and reconstruction of human civilization based on the natural-moral law principles of truth, justice, and nonaggression. It critiques the Western paradigm as Darwinian, animalistic, and inherently uncivilized, rooted in racism, statism, and structural injustice. It affirms that a society cannot be considered truly civilized if it systematically relies on coercion, deception, repression, and aggression—even if it is materially advanced. Africonomics asserts that moral development, not material progress, is the cornerstone and essence of human civilization. This paper contends that only fundamentally ethical and structurally just socioeconomic systems, grounded in natural-moral law, can lead to a genuinely civilized world. It concludes that Africonomics provides the intellectual and moral foundation for such a transformation, offering Africa the opportunity to lead a global rebirth of civilization.

title: The Invention of the "Ignorance Awareness Factor (अ)" - A Conceptual Frontier Notation for the "Awareness of Unknown" for Conscious Decision Making in Humans & Machines
affiliations: ODEFTO TECH PRIVATE LIMITED

detail.title: The Invention of the "Ignorance Awareness Factor (अ)" - A Conceptual Frontier Notation for the "Awareness of Unknown" for Conscious Decision Making in Humans & Machines

declarations.declarationOfInterest: no
declarations.ethicsApproval: None.
declarations.funderStatement: Funded by ODEFTO LABS

detail.abstract:
Ludwig Wittgenstein famously observed, “The limits of my language mean the limits of my world,” highlighting that most of our thought process is limited by boundaries of our language. Most of us rarely practice creative awareness of the opportunities around us because our vocabulary lacks the means to express our own ignorance in our daily life especially in our academics. In academics or any trainings programs, our focus is only on what is already known by others and has least focus on exploration and creative thinking. As students, we often internalise these concepts through rote memorisation-even now, in the age of AI and machine learning, when the sum of human knowledge is available at our fingertips 24/7. This era is not about memorisation blindly follow what already exists; it is about exploration and discovery.

To address this, I am pioneering a new field of study by introducing the dimension of awareness and ignorance by inventing a notation for Awareness of our Ignorance which paper covers in details. This aspect is almost entirely overlooked in existing literature, however all the geniuses operate with this frame of reference. By inventing a formal notation can be used in math and beyond math which works as a foundation of my future and past works helping a better human and machine decision making with awareness.

This paper proposes the introduction of the Ignorance Awareness Factor, denoted by the symbol 'अ', which is the first letter of “agyan” (अज्ञान) the Sanskrit word for ignorance. It is a foundational letter in many languages & most of the Indian languages, symbolising a starting point of our formal learning. This paves the way for a new universal language even to explore overall concept of consciousness: not just mathematics, but “MATH + Beyond Math,” capable of expressing both logical reasoning and the creative, emotional, and artistic dimensions of human understanding.

title: Antitrust Remedies and Data Privacy
affiliations: Temple University - James E. Beasley School of Law

detail.title: Antitrust Remedies and Data Privacy
detail.abstract:
This chapter explores the relationship between antitrust remedies and data privacy in U.S. law and policy. Part I begins with an introduction to the basics of U.S. antitrust law and remedies. Antitrust law works to restore and preserve competition, while U.S. data privacy law primarily seeks to provide individuals with control over the processing of their personal information. Competition and data privacy are increasingly intertwined in the digital economy, as data privacy law expands outward and antitrust law turns its attention to data-driven competition.

 

Part II considers antitrust remedies that purposefully seek to affect data privacy. It argues that antitrust courts and agencies are limited in their intervention into privacy by the relevance of the remedy to competition. These institutions have the power to impose antitrust remedies that restore privacy-based competition, but not to use litigated antitrust remedies to cure standalone privacy harms, unrelated to competition.

 

Part III then considers the unintended side effects that antitrust remedies may have on data privacy, both positive and negative. Even antitrust remedial orders that are not designed to impact data privacy may do so, by virtue of their intervention into how personal data is collected, used, or sold. This Part argues that antitrust institutions can and should design antitrust remedies to reduce unnecessary, negative side effects on data privacy. They have the power to do so, provided one important condition is met— the antitrust remedy remains effective in restoring or preserving competition, despite any accommodation of privacy interests.

title: The impact of discrimination on team performance in the white captain era of West Indian cricket
affiliations: University of Michigan at Ann Arbor

detail.title: The impact of discrimination on team performance in the white captain era of West Indian cricket

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: The West Indies, representing Caribbean islands and territories under British colonial rule, were granted cricket Test match status in 1928. Selection of the team was decided by the West Indies Cricket Board of Control, which was dominated by the wealthy white elites of the region. Although the teams were mixed, until 1960 the Board maintained a policy of only appointing white captains. This paper shows that the white captain policy imposed a cost on the team, because the average white player selected was not as good as the average nonwhite player. Based on performance statistics in matches which influenced selection decisions, it is shown that this underperformance was predictable. Finally, it is shown that if players had been selected on measurable indicators of ability alone, the average white Test player would have been substantially less likely to be selected than the average nonwhite Test player. This is consistent with Becker's concept of a taste for discrimination and its associated cost.

title: (Why) Have Financial Markets Become More Volatile? The Role of Market Index Trading
affiliations: and University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) - Anderson School of Management

detail.title: (Why) Have Financial Markets Become More Volatile? The Role of Market Index Trading
detail.abstract: We document a persistent doubling of U.S. stock market volatility since the mid-20th century, which cannot be attributed to macroeconomic fundamentals or idiosyncratic firm shocks. Instead, we show that the increased volume and dominance of index trading-via futures, ETFs, and extended trading hours-has structurally raised aggregate stock market volatility. We exploit the introduction of E-mini S&P 500 futures and historical NYSE trading-hour adjustments as natural experiments to provide causal evidence that index-level trading amplifies market variance through trading volume. Our model of index demand shocks rationalizes these findings, predicting higher market-level volatility, reduced return autocorrelation, and an increased share of systematic risk. Fluctuations in asset prices and volatility are increasingly determined by technology and trading structure rather than fundamentals.

title: Geopolitical Risk and Inflation Heterogeneity in the Euro Area
affiliations: University of Pavia, Sciences Po and European Central Bank (ECB) - Directorate General Research

detail.title: Geopolitical Risk and Inflation Heterogeneity in the Euro Area
detail.abstract: Using quarterly data for nineteen euro area countries since 2000, we show that geopolitical shocks raise consumer and producer prices, with stronger and more persistent effects on core inflation. War-related shocks generate inflation through supply-chain disruptions and trade linkages, whereas terrorism-related shocks produce mild, short-lived disinflationary effects. The impact is larger in more open and import-dependent economies. To interpret these findings, we develop a small open economy model and a monetary union model that together reveal how trade exposure, country size, and a common monetary policy shape the transmission of external shocks. In the union, larger and more integrated members amplify spillovers, while smaller or less connected economies remain insulated. Geopolitical risk thus emerges as a structural source of inflationary pressure and heterogeneity, complicating monetary policy in an increasingly fragmented global economy.

title: A Comprehensive Comparative Study on Educational Approaches for College Students Majoring in International Trade Operations Between China and the United States
affiliations: George Mason University

detail.title: A Comprehensive Comparative Study on Educational Approaches for College Students Majoring in International Trade Operations Between China and the United States

declarations.ethicsApproval: No ethics issue in this article.

detail.abstract: This research offers a detailed comparison of educational characteristics between the Chinese and American universities on International Trade Operations (ITO) college students. From historical developments, through to curriculum structures, pedagogical philosophies, internship management and graduate outcomes the paper exposes commonalities as well differences in the two nations approaches to equipping future professionals for the demands of global commerce. The discussion continues to consider the roles of cultural values, policy orientations and labour market dynamics in educational design and learning results. The study ends with a cooperative pedagogical model developed to synergize two unique systems in order to cultivate an international awareness of trade and intercultural capacity for graduates. This more specific information can inform policy makers, educators and administrators interested in advancing international business education and long-term cross-border collaboration. Simultaneously, this study also undertakes a thorough comparative analysis of the educational strategies employed by higher education institutions in China and the United States to prepare college students for careers in International Trade Operations (ITO). By examining historical trajectories, curriculum frameworks, pedagogical paradigms, integration of internships, assessment mechanisms, and post-graduation trajectories, the research delineates notable similarities and stark contrasts in how these two economic powerhouses cultivate expertise for the intricate demands of global commerce. The investigation delves into the profound influences of cultural underpinnings, governmental policies, and fluctuating labor market conditions on the architecture of educational programs and their resultant learning achievements. Drawing on empirical data and scholarly insights, this paper illuminates how China's emphasis on pragmatic, policy-aligned training complements the U.S.'s focus on innovative, interdisciplinary inquiry, yet both grapple with contemporary challenges like digital disruption and geopolitical tensions.

title: Hourly Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Using Exponential Smoothing: A Comparative Study Based on Operational Data
affiliations: Institute of General Energy of NAS of Ukraine, Institute of General Energy of NAS of Ukraine, Institute of General Energy of the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine, Independent and Institute of General Energy of NAS of Ukraine

detail.title: Hourly Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Using Exponential Smoothing: A Comparative Study Based on Operational Data

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by projects “Integrated modeling for robust management of food-energy-water-social-environmental (FEWSE) nexus security and sustainable development” (IIASA-NASU, 22-501 (R-45-T)), “Comprehensive analysis of robust preventive and adaptive measures of food, energy, water and social management in the context of systemic risks and consequences of COVID-19” (0122U000552, 2022–2026), “Development of the structure and ensuring the functioning of self-sufficient distributed generation” (0125U001572, 2025–2026), which are financed by National Academy of Science of Ukraine.

detail.abstract: The accurate forecasting of solar power generation is becoming increasingly important in the context of renewable energy integration and intelligent energy management. The variability of solar radiation, caused by changing meteorological conditions and diurnal cycles, complicates the planning and control of photovoltaic systems and may lead to imbalances in supply and demand. This study aims to identify the most effective exponential smoothing approach for real-world PV power forecasting using actual hourly generation data from a 9 MW solar power plant in the Kyiv region, Ukraine. Four exponential smoothing techniques are analysed: Classic, a Modified classic adapted to daily generation patterns, Holt's linear trend method, and the Holt-Winters seasonal method. The models were implemented in Microsoft Excel (Microsoft 365, version 2408) using real measurement data collected over six months. Forecasts were generated one hour ahead, and optimal smoothing constants were identified via RMSE minimisation using the Solver Add-in. Substantial differences in forecasting accuracy were observed. The Classic simple exponential smoothing model performed worst, with an RMSE of 1413.58 kW and nMAE of 9.22%. Holt's method improved trend responsiveness (RMSE = 1052.79 kW, nMAE = 5.96%), but still lacked seasonality modelling. Holt-Winters, which incorporates both trend and seasonality, achieved a strong balance (RMSE = 1031.00 kW, nMAE = 3.7%). The best performance was observed with the modified simple exponential smoothing method, which captured the daily cycle more effectively (RMSE = 166.45 kW, nMAE = 0.84%). These results pertain to a one-step-ahead evaluation on a single plant and an extended validation window; accuracy is dependent on meteorological conditions, with larger errors during rapid cloud transi. The study identifies forecasting models that combine high accuracy with structural simplicity, intuitive implementation, and minimal parameter tuning-features that make them well-suited for integration into lightweight real-time energy control systems, despite not being evaluated in terms of runtime or memory usage. The modified simple exponential smoothing model, in particular, offers a high degree of precision and interpretability, supporting its integration into operational PV forecasting tools.

title: Riskier Together? The Effect of Combined Tax Reporting on Corporate Risk-Taking
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Riskier Together? The Effect of Combined Tax Reporting on Corporate Risk-Taking
detail.abstract: To constrain tax-motivated income shifting, many U.S. states have adopted combined tax reporting, which effectively requires affiliated corporations under common ownership to compute taxable income on a consolidated basis rather than a separate-entity basis. I examine whether combined reporting has an unintended effect on firm risk-taking. I find that after a state adopts combined reporting, affected firms report higher earnings volatility and R&D expenditures compared to unaffected firms. The results from cross-sectional tests are consistent with combined reporting increasing firm risk-taking by enhancing tax loss offset capabilities. The effects are smaller in patent-intensive income-shifting firms, consistent with combined reporting's antiincome shifting feature reducing the after-tax payoffs of producing intangible property. Collectively, the evidence offers nuance to existing research, which suggests tax rate increases and anti-income shifting policies negatively affect risk-taking and innovative activities. The results are particularly relevant given increased combined reporting legislation by U.S. states and similar international proposals.

title: Success factors for young science and technology parks.
affiliations: Kingston University - School of Computer Science and Mathematics, Kingston University and Kingston University

detail.title: Success factors for young science and technology parks.

contentFormat.other: Full paper of a conference abstract

detail.abstract: This paper presents some novel-seeming concepts derived from new data-driven approaches. An overview of studies on the organic growth of young start-up Science and Technology Parks (STP), using Big Data, econometric analyses, panel data and computer simulations is presented. Results and concepts derived from industrialised countries, notably Sweden and the UK, may well be applicable to some emerging economies. Results are of interest to technology entrepreneurs considering choosing a STP to inhabit, as well as those in the central team, specialising in management and enterprise development, including growing new Parks.

title: When State Concessions Backfire: Information Cascades, Protest Mobilization, and Authoritarian Survival
affiliations: , Hitotsubashi University - Graduate School of Economics and Princeton University

detail.title: When State Concessions Backfire: Information Cascades, Protest Mobilization, and Authoritarian Survival
detail.abstract: Do a dictator's concessions demobilize protests or instead fuel mobilization that threatens regime survival? To address this question, we develop a two-period model of protest cascades in which vanguards first decide whether to initiate protests, followed by ordinary citizens who choose whether to join. Concessions directly reduce incentives to protest, but they also make a vanguard's protest a stronger signal of regime weakness. As a result, concessions lower the likelihood of vanguard protests while paradoxically increasing ordinary citizens' propensity to follow once protests occur. We show that concessions raise the probability of regime change when (i) vanguards enjoy a sufficiently large advantage over ordinary citizens in participation costs and information, and (ii) when the regime is relatively resilient, that is, it has low vulnerability to protest and a mild commitment problem. Beyond theory, we also derive testable predictions and discuss empirical implications for research on contentious politics and comparative authoritarianism.

title: Constrained Mediation: Bayesian Implementability of Joint Posteriors
affiliations: Ben Gurion University of the Negev and Durham University Business School

detail.title: Constrained Mediation: Bayesian Implementability of Joint Posteriors

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We have no relevant or material financial interests that relate to the research described in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: Lagziel acknowledges the support of the Israel Science Foundation, Grant #2074/23. Lehrer acknowledges the support of the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation) -- Project Number 461570745.

detail.abstract: We examine information structures in settings with privately informed agents and an informationally constrained mediator who supplies additional public signals. Our focus is on characterizing the set of posteriors that the mediator can induce. To this end, we employ a graph-theoretic framework: states are represented as vertices, information sets correspond to edges, and a likelihood ratio function on edges encodes the posterior beliefs. Within this framework, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions, internal and external consistency, for the rationalization of posteriors. Finally, we identify conditions under which a single mediator can implement multiple posteriors, effectively serving as a generator of Blackwell experiments.

title: Sample Size Neglect and Biases in Beliefs: Evidence from the Field
affiliations: University of Warwick - Warwick Business School, University of Warwick - Warwick Business School and University of Surrey - Surrey Business School

detail.title: Sample Size Neglect and Biases in Beliefs: Evidence from the Field
detail.abstract: Larger samples provide precise estimates, reducing variability around the true value. We examine whether sophisticated agents adhere to this foundational statistical principle when forming beliefs in a real-world, high-stakes setting. Specifically, we use tennis betting markets as a quasi-natural laboratory that offers three key advantages: bookmakers are highly incentivized professionals; their beliefs can be directly inferred from their quoted odds; and match length varies exogenously across tournaments, playing a role analogous to sample size, as longer matches reduce randomness, making outcomes more reliably reflective of underlying skill. We find that professional bookmakers exhibit sample size neglect, leading to systematic biases in their beliefs and lower profits. A laboratory experiment shows that this bias is twice as large among students, who are less sophisticated with lower incentives than bookmakers, and weaker when the effect of sample size on underlying probabilities becomes more salient. Finally, extending to financial markets, we show that while the consensus analyst forecast is more predictive of earnings when based on more analysts, stock prices seem to underreact to the component of forecasts attributable to analyst coverage. Overall, our results suggest that sample size neglect leads to systematic biases in the beliefs of sophisticated agents even in relatively simple settings.

title: Consumer Control in Competitive Markets
affiliations: University of Calgary

detail.title: Consumer Control in Competitive Markets

declarations.funderStatement: SSHRC

detail.abstract: We study buyer-controlled disclosure in a duopoly with differentiated products where multiproduct sellers recommend products. Greater disclosure precision leads to more accurate recommendations and makes compared options closer in expected fit, intensifying competition. Consequently, the buyer reveals her preference information with full precision in equilibrium, and welfare outcomes under commitment (uniform prices) and no-commitment (personalized prices) pricing regimes coincide. This contrasts with monopoly settings, where the seller prefers commitment and the buyer is harmed. Our findings suggest policy should prioritize buyer-controlled disclosure mechanisms with granular precision controls, as this steers recommendations toward better matches and organizes competition around identified preferences.

title: Brief of Amici Curiae in Support of Appellant and Reversal; Cargill v. Garland 57 F.4th 447 (5th Cir. 2023).
affiliations: FPC Action Foundation, University of Wyoming College of Law and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Brief of Amici Curiae in Support of Appellant and Reversal; Cargill v. Garland 57 F.4th 447 (5th Cir. 2023).
detail.abstract:
Chevron deference is neither a standard nor a tool of interpretation. Rather, it is a description of a presumed congressional delegation of legislative decision-making authority to an agency and a framework for evaluating the consequences of such presumed delegation. So understood, the relation between Chevron deference, the rule of lenity, and how to address an executive agency’s failure to exercise delegated legislative authority illuminates proper resolution of agency actions involving criminal penalties. Implied delegations of legislative authority are suspect where the premise of such implication is a congressional failure to use clear statutory language, thus “requiring” an executive branch agency to make legislative policy decisions. This suspicion should become prohibitive where a statute bearing criminal penalties is involved.

This Court need not defer to an executive agency’s interpretation where, as here, there is an applicable canon of construction that guides this Court’s hand in removing ambiguity—or at least resolving ambiguity—from the statute in question. Given this matter involves a criminal penalty, if the Court determines there is ambiguity in the definition of “machinegun,” then this Court should resolve that ambiguity in favor of the individual, not the executive agency, under the rule of lenity.

Finally, Chevron deference is wholly inapplicable in matters involving the interpretation of newly created crimes, given it violates our Constitution’s separation of powers. An executive agency cannot be allowed to create criminal laws through “interpretation” of “vague” statutes, enforce its own newly created law, and then receive judicial deference as to the evaluation of the agency’s authority, construction, and enforcement.

This Court should remand this matter to the district court with instructions for that court to review the plain meaning of the term “machinegun,” and if ambiguous, to resolve that ambiguity by applying the rule of lenity, not Chevron deference.

title: Business Concentration in China: 1978-2023
affiliations: Fudan University - China Center for Economic Studies (CCES) and Fudan University - China Center for Economic Studies (CCES)

detail.title: Business Concentration in China: 1978-2023
detail.abstract: This paper studies the evolution of business concentration in China from 1978 to 2023. We combine rich administrative data to provide consistent series of the top 1 percent share among industrial and service firms. We find that industrial concentration has undergone fluctuations in multiple stages, driven by the exit of inefficient state-owned firms under the top-down reform, and by the emergence of high-markup private firms from bottom up. Meanwhile, concentration in the service sector has steadily increased until stagnating in the last five years, primarily reflecting the rise and fall of large firms in the trade and real estate sectors. (JEL L11, M21, O14)

title: Freedoms, Agency, and Fundamental Rights in Colombia Freedoms, Agency and Rights
affiliations: EDUKIVOTOS

detail.title: Freedoms, Agency, and Fundamental Rights in Colombia Freedoms, Agency and Rights
detail.abstract: This article analyzes the relationship between Amartya Sen 's theory of freedoms , conceived as both an end and a means of human development, and Title II of the 1991 Colombian Political Constitution , relating to rights, guarantees, and duties. It examines how the Constitution enshrines the expansion of real freedoms as the core of development and whether the country's legal and political structures allow for their practical implementation. From a qualitative, normative, and comparative approach , the correspondence between constitutional rights and Sen's categories of agency, choice, and human capabilities is studied. The results show that, although the 1991 Constitution incorporates the ethical vision of development as freedom, social inequality, corruption, and territorial exclusion limit its effectiveness. The article concludes that the challenge for the Colombian State is to transform formal freedoms into real freedoms that allow each person to be an agent of their own development.

title: Tax Incentives and Firm Compliance: Evidence from China *
affiliations: Fudan University - China Center for Economic Studies (CCES), Fudan University - China Center for Economic Studies (CCES), Fudan University - China Center for Economic Studies (CCES) and Ocean University of China

detail.title: Tax Incentives and Firm Compliance: Evidence from China *
detail.abstract: We examine how tax policy affects firm compliance, drawing on a 2003 enforcement campaign in Chongqing, China. Local officials promoted a preferential corporate income tax rate treatment(15% versus 33%) under the Western Development Project through door-to-door visits. Using a difference-indifferences design, we find that firms became more likely to report positive profits at the extensive margin, leading to higher declared profits and tax payments. For newly compliant firms, the increases came from reported sales and costs rather than real growth in investment or employment. In contrast, consistently compliant firms raised investment and employment, while output did not increase significantly in the short run. Overall, these responses boosted local fiscal revenue by about 20 percent. The findings show that compliance can be strengthened not only by deterrence but also by credible and favorable tax regimes.

title: Revisiting Land, Labor, and Capital in Neoclassical Economics
affiliations: CNRS, CIRED and Centre International de Recherche sur l'Environnement et le Développement

detail.title: Revisiting Land, Labor, and Capital in Neoclassical Economics

declarations.funderStatement: European Research Council (101040475)

detail.abstract: It is usually argued that the advent of neoclassical economics led to the consideration of only two factors of production (capital and labor) instead of three (capital, labor, and land). From the 1880s to the 1920s, land and natural resources would have been marginalized and left to applied fields such as land economics. This article revisits this episode. Theoretically, it shows that there was no requirement in marginal productivity theories to subsume land into capital. Historically, it demonstrates that alternatives did exist within U.S. neoclassicism to the neglect of land and natural resources, providing inspiration for today's research. (JEL B13, Q24)

title: ESG-XAI: An Explainable Unsupervised Feature Selection Pipeline for ESG Datasets
affiliations: Singapore University of Social Sciences, Singapore University of Social Sciences and

detail.title: ESG-XAI: An Explainable Unsupervised Feature Selection Pipeline for ESG Datasets

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No potential competing interest was reported by the authors.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable (study uses publicly disclosed firm-level ESG data).
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received.

detail.abstract: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) panels are difficult to model. Variables live on mixed scales, redundancy within silos is high, cross-silo alignment is weak, and labels suitable for supervision are scarce or disputed. We present a deployment-ready, end-to-end workflow that turns such disclosure matrices into train-only labels for evaluation, out-of-sample performance estimates, and audit-ready explanations that trace back to ESG indicators. The system separates three planes-Discovery, Prediction, and Explanation-with strict train/test boundaries. Discovery builds a balanced multi-view latent (per-silo PCA-fusion) and uses evidence accumulation with stability rule to choose the number of segments (minimizing Proportion of Ambiguous Clustering). When global discovery is weak, an evaluation-feasibility guard constructs label-agnostic, stratified base splits and defers labeling to training folds. Prediction adopts nested labeling with nearest-centroid assignment to test, closing common leakage paths. Explanation is fold-local; we select a balanced set of features per silo on the training fold and compute SHAP only on held-out tests. On a 2024 ESG panel (57 firms; 61 indicators: E=15, S=25, G=21), 2D linear discriminants (PCA/NCA-LDA) attain balanced accuracy ≈ 0.917, with low dispersion under strict nested evaluation, outperforming higher-capacity baselines. Performance remains stable when raw clusterings vary. Fold-local explanations with human-interpretable drivers indicate social variables as dominant contributors, followed by environmental and governance. The study contributes a portable, auditable ESG analytics pipeline allows evaluation when discovery is weak, reduces model risk, and delivers transparent outputs suitable for ESG use cases in small-𝑛 settings.

title: Gambling with Dividends
affiliations: University of Kiel - Institute for Quantitative Business and Economics Research (QBER), University of Mannheim, University of Kiel - Institute for Quantitative Business and Economics Research (QBER) and University of Mannheim - Department of Banking and Finance

detail.title: Gambling with Dividends
detail.abstract: Previous research suggests that many investors view dividends as free income. In this paper, we show that this fallacy can drive investors to gamble with dividends. First, using brokerage data, we document that investors use disproportionate fractions of dividends to buy lottery stocks and options. Second, using an experiment, we replicate the tendency to gamble with dividends in the lab and find that this tendency is stronger among participants suffering from the free dividends fallacy. Third, using stock market data, we test asset pricing implications and show that marketwide dividends are associated with price pressure in lottery stocks.

title: Moment-Based Confidence Intervals Under Dependence And Jumps
affiliations: VinUniversity

detail.title: Moment-Based Confidence Intervals Under Dependence And Jumps
detail.abstract: We propose a unified framework for constructing confidence intervals for moment-based estimators in the presence of serial dependence and jumps. The approach builds on the joint asymptotic distribution of sample moments and applies the multivariate Delta method to propagate the long-run covariance structure to any smooth function of moments, including the mean, variance, skewness, and kurtosis. This yields augmented confidence intervals that remain valid under temporal dependence and discontinuous dynamics, providing a coherent extension of standard i.i.d. inference to non-Gaussian environments. A key contribution is the derivation of closed-form sample-size formulas linking the precision of moment estimators to long-run dependence and jump intensity. These expressions quantify how volatility clustering and rare but large shocks inflate estimator variance and dramatically increase the data required for reliable inference. Overall, the framework delivers a general, model-free foundation for dependence-and jump-robust inference across all empirical moments, unifying confidence interval construction and sample-size determination within a single, covariance-based Delta-method formulation.

title: Thin Capitalization and Firm's Financial Performance: Are Older Firms at an Advantage?
affiliations: University of Calabar, University of Nigeria, Nsukka, University of Nigeria, University of Calabar, University of Calabar, University of Calabar, University of Calabar and University of Nigeria

detail.title: Thin Capitalization and Firm's Financial Performance: Are Older Firms at an Advantage?
detail.abstract: This study examined effect of thin capitalization on the financial performance of listed multinational firms in Nigeria for a period of 18 years (2006 to 2023). The Specific objectives were to: examine the effect of debt-to-equity ratio(DER) on return on capital employed(ROCE) of multinational corporations in Nigeria, ascertain the effect of Interest cover ratio (ICR) on return on capital employed of multinational corporations in Nigeria, evaluate the effect of Debt-to-asset ratio(DTA) on return on capital employed of multinational corporations in Nigeria, determine the moderating effect of firm age on the relationship between thin capitalization and financial performance of multinational corporations in Nigeria. Ex-post facto research design was adopted. The study used secondary sources of data from financial statements of the selected companies under study. The population of the study consisted of all 19 multinational firms listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group as at December 2023.The sampling technique used for this study was the purposive non probability sampling technique, 16 firms which represents approximately 85%of the entire population were used as the sample size, the other 3 firms were dropped based on data unavailability, while the analytical technique used for the study was panel least square regression model. Results of the study shows that the predictor variables examined (DAR, ICR) except (DER) have no significant effect on the financial performance of MNCs in Nigeria measured by (ROCE). Lastly, firm age moderates the relationship between DER and DAR as proxies of thin capitalization and ROCE as a measure of financial performance. The study concluded that thin capitalization has a negative significant effect on the performance of listed multinational firms in Nigeria and recommends amongst others that management of multinational companies in Nigeria should not contract excessive debt from affiliates as the interest payments may not significantly reduce their tax liabilities or positively enhance performance. Also, older firms are more at an advantage if they engage in thin capitalization practices as against younger firms.

title: Text Is All You Need: Asset Pricing Without Returns
affiliations: Technische Universität München (TUM) - TUM School of Management

detail.title: Text Is All You Need: Asset Pricing Without Returns
detail.abstract: How should investors value firms without return histories? When trading data are missing, investors typically rely on industry betas as coarse proxies for systematic risk, introducing valuation errors whenever firm-specific exposures differ from peer norms. Using IPOs as a natural laboratory, I show that textual risk disclosures can substitute for missing return data. I develop Aggregated Cluster Embeddings (ACE), which convert qualitative risk narratives into structured firm-level representations. Disclosure-based betas reduce market beta prediction errors by up to 27 percent relative to standard benchmarks (industry betas). However, investors underweight this information at issuance, and firms whose disclosures imply lower risk than their industry peers are initially undervalued, yielding monthly six-factor alphas of 97 basis points. These excess returns fade as return histories accumulate, consistent with markets gradually learning firm-specific covariances. The results highlight a mechanism of information substitution and investor inattention in pricing firms without trading histories.
